newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end down sharply as longs bail.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end down sharply as longs bail.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Thursday in a moderate session, with front months pressured sharply as longs scrambled to liquidate after Wednesday's bearish AGA report, sources said.
November tumbled 9.9 cents to close at $2.371 per million British thermal units. December was 8.9 cents lower at $2.515. Others ended down by 1.2 to 9.6 cents.

"Storage is a non-event in the East and everything now depends on weather. We are going to get some colder weather from Detroit to Boston, but by the end of next week, the weather support isn't there," said one Midwest trader.

Most agreed technical selling after recent gains coupled with a bearish AGA report Wednesday triggered the flood of long liquidation today. But they said further downside may be limited near-term by a cold front that should prop up the cash.

Chartists pegged support in November in the $2.30 area, with resistance seen at Wednesday's high of $2.59 and then in the mid-$2.60s, a measurement objective after the break last week of a head-and-shoulders bottom formation.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices firmed more than five cents Thursday to the high-$2.30s, about 55 cents over October indices. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly at about the $2.20 level, about 50 cents over October 1 levels. New York city gate gas was quoted five cents higher in the mid-$2.60s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 2.8 cents to $2.204. NYMEX said 44,787 Hub contracts traded, up from Wednesday's revised tally of 59,960.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled 4.5 cents lower at $1.07, while deferreds closed down by one-half to 4.5 cents.
NYMEX November Permian natgas finished down 5.5 cents at $2.055, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 56 Permian lots changed hands compared to no trading on Wednesday.
On the KCBT, November settled eight cents lower at $2.11, while deferreds ended down by six to 8.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.9 cents to 26.1 cents (NYMEX premium).
